journal.title: Why a trading journal changes everything
journal.bodyHtml:
Most losing traders don't fail from lack of strategy — they fail because they have no reliable memory of their decisions. Without a journal, every trade is an isolated anecdote. With a structured trading journal, your trades become data — and data reveals patterns your memory systematically hides.

Your brain remembers spectacular wins and erases small repeated mistakes. That's the opposite of what you need to improve. A journal fixes this bias by recording every entry, exit, position size and emotion felt.

What a good journal gives you

  • Objectivity: you judge your trading on numbers, not gut feel.
  • Leak detection: setups that look good but cost you money over 50 trades.
  • Reinforcing what works: you find your real edge and focus capital there.
  • Accountability: hard to lie to yourself with a timestamped history.

Essential fields to log

An effective journal isn't just P&L. Log the asset, session, setup, planned risk/reward, whether you followed your plan, and your mental state at entry. It's the combination of these dimensions that makes analysis powerful.

With Paychek, these fields are prefilled and standardized: you journal in seconds instead of maintaining a fragile spreadsheet abandoned after two weeks.

analyse.title: How to analyze your trades and actually improve
analyse.bodyHtml:
Keeping a journal is step one; analysis turns history into progress. But beware: some metrics flatter your ego without reflecting real profitability.

Metrics that matter

  • Expectancy: average expected gain per trade. The queen metric — it combines win rate and R/R.
  • Risk/reward ratio: how much you make when right vs. lose when wrong.
  • Win rate by setup: a global rate means nothing; segment by strategy and session.
  • Max drawdown: the worst losing streak your psychology must survive.

The win rate trap

A 70% win rate can hide an emptying account if losses are three times larger than wins. Conversely, a trader at 40% with a 1:3 ratio is highly profitable. Never look at win rate alone — always pair it with R/R and expectancy.

Segment, segment, segment

Real progress comes from segmentation. Are you better in the morning or afternoon? On forex or indices? On breakouts or mean reversion? A journal that filters stats by asset, session and setup shows exactly where to focus capital — and what to stop immediately.

psychologie.title: Trader psychology: discipline before strategy
psychologie.bodyHtml:
Most avoidable losses come not from bad analysis but undisciplined execution: entering too early, moving stops, doubling down on losers, cutting winners from fear. Psychology isn't fluff — it's the decisive factor.

Emotions that destroy accounts

  • Fear: you cut winners too early and miss your best trades.
  • Greed: you oversize positions and ignore your plan.
  • Revenge: after a loss, you trade to "get even" and the spiral accelerates.
  • Boredom: you take mediocre trades just to be in a position.

Measure discipline, not just feelings

You only fix what you measure. By noting for each trade whether you followed your plan and your mental state, you get a discipline score. Over weeks, you see clearly how emotional slips correlate with losses — often more effective than any advice.

Paychek includes mindset tracking and a discipline audit: your emotions become measurable — and improvable — data.

import.title: Import your trades (MT4, MT5, CSV) without wasting time
import.bodyHtml:
The best journal is the one you actually keep. If entry is painful, you'll quit. That's why automatic import is a game-changer: it removes friction and keeps data consistent.

Manual entry vs import

Manual entry still helps for context (your reasoning, mental state, chart screenshot). But for factual data — entry, exit, size, P&L — importing from your broker statement is faster and more reliable.

Supported formats

  • MT4 / MT5: import statements and let the app rebuild each position.
  • CSV: most brokers and platforms (futures, crypto, equities) export standard CSV.
  • FIFO reconstruction: partial fills are grouped into coherent trades automatically.

Save time for what matters

The goal isn't an hour copying numbers — it's analysis and improvement. By automating import, you keep a complete journal effortlessly and turn data collection into lasting statistical edge.
